key_insight: Calibrated Partial Resets (CPR) preserves neural plasticity in continual learning by gently pulling low-utility neurons back toward initialization instead of fully reinitializing them, reducing policy collapse while maintaining performance.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical stability-plasticity control mechanism for reinforcement learning systems deployed in non-stationary environments where long-horizon adaptation is critical.
method: Periodically identify low-utility neurons during training.
Apply partial, utility-scaled resets toward each neuron's initialization.
Use calibrated strength to target stale units while avoiding destabilizing full resets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that CPR avoided policy collapse over 400M training steps in SlipperyAnt and outperformed prior decay- and reset-based methods on Continual MetaWorld and Continual MinAtar.
watch_item: The reset strength and utility threshold likely require careful tuning, since the method explicitly trades off plasticity against peak performance.
paper_title: Calibrated Partial Resets: Preventing Policy Collapse in Continual Reinforcement Learning
